title: The past tense
intro: A2 opens with the past: what you did yesterday, last week or two days ago. One suffix, `-dY`, makes the past of every verb (*geldim*, I came; *okadyk*, we read), with its own short set of personal endings. This unit adds the negative and questions (*gelmedim*, *geldiňmi?*), puts the two sets of endings side by side, and gives you the time words that go with the past: *düýn*, *öňňin*, *geçen hepde*, *iki gün öň*, *eýýäm*, *entek*.

sections.title: I came, we read: the past in -dY

blocks.text: To say what happened and is over, add `-dY` to the stem ([A1 unit 6](a1-u06)): *-dy* after a back vowel, *-di* after a front one. Then add the ending for the person: *gel-* → *geldim*, I came; *oka-* → *okadyk*, we read. With no ending it is **he**, **she** or **it**: *geldi*, she came.

**The d never changes.** Whatever sound the stem ends in, the past starts with *d*: *gitdi* (went), *aýtdy* (said), *içdi* (drank), *ýazdy* (wrote). And because *d* is a consonant, the verbs that turn *t* into *d* before `-ýAr` keep their *t* here: *gidýär* but *gitdi*, *edýär* but *etdi*, *aýdýar* but *aýtdy*. A stem ending in *e* keeps its *e*: *işledi*, *diňledi*.

**Rounding.** After a first syllable with *o, ö, u* or *ü*, the vowel of the second syllable rounds to *u* or *ü*, unless it ends the word ([A1 unit 2](a1-u02)): *gördüm* (I saw) but *gördi* (she saw), *boldum* but *boldy*. From the third syllable on there is no rounding: *okadym*, *oturdym*.

As in the present, the ending says who, so the pronoun can be left out: *Okadym* is **I read** on its own. With *olar*, the *-lAr* can be dropped when the pronoun is said: *Olar geldi* or *Olar geldiler*.

blocks.title: -m, not -yn
blocks.text: The past has its own endings: **I came** is *geldim*, not `geldin`, and **we came** is *geldik*. Mind the *ň* of **you**: *geldiň*, you came.

sections.title: I didn't come; did you? Negative and questions

blocks.text: For the negative, put `-mA` (*-ma* or *-me*) between the stem and `-dY`, as in the present: *gel-me-di-m*, I didn't come; *oka-ma-dy*, she didn't read. The personal endings stay the same.

rows.en: he, she or it didn't come

blocks.text: **Questions.** Add `-mY` after the personal ending, all in one word: *Geldiňmi?* Did you come? *Geldimi?* Did he come? *Okadyňyzmy?* Did you read it? For a negative question, the same particle goes after the negative form: *Gelmediňmi?* Didn't you come?

rows.en: Did he, she or it come?
Didn't he, she or it come?

items.en: Yes, I did. (Yes, I read it.)

blocks.text: **Short answers** repeat the verb, not a word like **did**: *Geldiňmi? — Hawa, geldim* (Yes, I did) or *Ýok, gelmedim* (No, I didn't).

blocks.title: The particle comes last
blocks.text: In the past the question particle always follows the personal ending: *geldiňmi*, *okadyňyzmy*. It is written onto the verb, not apart: *geldiňmi*, not `geldiň mi`.

You now know two sets of endings for the person. The first came with the present and the formal **to be**: *gelýärin*, *talypdyryn*. The second comes with the past: *geldim*. The **he, she, it** form has no ending in both, and **they** takes `-lAr` in both. The other four persons differ.

blocks.text: The second set is the short one, a single consonant in the singular: **I** is *-m*, **you** *-ň*, **we** *-k*. If it helps, *-m* and *-ň* are the same sounds as **my** and **your** in *kitabym*, *kitabyň* ([A1 unit 9](a1-u09)).

items.en: I'm working today, and I worked yesterday too.

blocks.title: Don't mix the sets
blocks.text: Each tense has its own set: *gelýärin* and *geldim*, never `gelýärim` or `geldin`. If the verb has *-ýAr*, use the first set; if it has *-dY*, the second.

sections.title: Yesterday, last week, two days ago

blocks.text: These words place an action in the past. Like other time words, they usually come early in the sentence, before or after the subject, and the verb stays at the end: *Men düýn işledim* or *Düýn men işledim*.

*geçen* means **last**, the one that has passed: *geçen hepde*, *geçen şenbe* (last Saturday). For **ago**, put *öň* after the length of time: *iki gün öň* (two days ago), *bir sagat öň* (an hour ago), *bäş ýyl öň* (five years ago). After a number the noun stays singular, as always: *iki gün*, not `iki günler`.

*eýýäm* (already) and *ýaňy* (just) go with a positive verb: *Awtobus eýýäm gitdi* (The bus has already left), *Men ýaňy geldim* (I've just arrived). *entek* (yet) goes with a negative: *Men entek nahar iýmedim* (I haven't eaten yet). English uses **has** and **have** here; Turkmen just uses the past.

items.en: The day before yesterday we went to Dashoguz.
Last week Aýna went to Mary.
The child has already fallen asleep.

blocks.title: Has done, did
blocks.text: English chooses between **I ate** and **I have eaten**. Turkmen has one past for both here: *Men nahar iýdim* answers **Did you eat?** and **Have you eaten?** alike. Time words such as *eýýäm*, *ýaňy* and *entek* carry the extra meaning.

blocks.title: öň after the time
blocks.text: **Ago** comes after the span: *iki gün öň*, not `öň iki gün`. And **last week** is *geçen hepde*, with no ending on *hepde*.

summary: The past is stem + `-dY` (*-dy, -di*, or *-du, -dü* by the rounding rule) + the second set of endings: *-m, -ň, —, -k, -ňYz, -lAr*: *geldim, okadyň, gördi, gitdik*.
The *d* never changes, and *t*-verbs keep their *t*: *gitdi*, *etdi*, *aýtdy*.
Negative: `-mA` before `-dY`: *gelmedim*. Question: `-mY` after the ending: *geldiňmi?*, *gelmediňmi?*
The first set (*-Yn, -sYň, -Ys, -sYňYz*) goes with the present; the second (*-m, -ň, -k, -ňYz*) with the past.
Time words: *düýn, öňňin, geçen hepde, iki gün öň*; *eýýäm* and *ýaňy* with a positive verb, *entek* with a negative.
